import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# According to operation_history: UNION of all source tables
# All source tables have the same schema: ['State Name', 'AQI', 'Year', 'Month']
# Target schema: ['State Name': string, 'Year': int, 'Month': int, 'AQI': int]
# Reorder columns to match target schema and ensure correct dtypes

# Concatenate all source DataFrames (union)
union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Reorder columns to target schema order
union_df = union_df[['State Name', 'Year', 'Month', 'AQI']]

# Ensure correct data types
union_df['State Name'] = union_df['State Name'].astype(str)
union_df['Year'] = union_df['Year'].astype(int)
union_df['Month'] = union_df['Month'].astype(int)
union_df['AQI'] = union_df['AQI'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/target_multisource.csv"
union_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all sources on ['State Name', 'Year', 'Month']
# Since all sources have the same schema, and target schema is the same,
# but the failed pipeline did a UNION causing 80000 rows instead of 2273,
# we join on the key columns to combine AQI values per State Name, Year, Month.

# First join source0 and source1
join01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# Then join with source2
join012 = pd.merge(join01, source2, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer')

# The last join with source3
# source2 columns: ['State Name', 'AQI', 'Year', 'Month']
# After merge with source1 and source0, AQI columns are suffixed or original
# To avoid confusion, rename AQI columns accordingly before next merge

# Rename AQI columns for clarity
join012 = join012.rename(columns={'AQI': 'AQI_2'})

join_final = pd.merge(join012, source3, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer', suffixes=('', '_3'))

# Now we have AQI columns: AQI_0, AQI_1, AQI_2, AQI (from source3)
# Rename AQI from source0 and source1 to AQI_0 and AQI_1 respectively
# But source0 AQI is AQI_0, source1 AQI is AQI_1, source2 AQI is AQI_2, source3 AQI is AQI (no suffix)

# Actually, after first merge, AQI columns are AQI_0 and AQI_1
# After second merge, AQI from source2 is AQI (no suffix)
# After third merge, AQI from source3 is AQI_3 (due to suffixes)

# Let's fix the AQI columns naming properly:

# After first merge (source0 and source1)
join01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# After second merge (join01 and source2)
join012 = pd.merge(join01, source2, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer')
join012 = join012.rename(columns={'AQI': 'AQI_2'})

# After third merge (join012 and source3)
join_final = pd.merge(join012, source3, on=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month'], how='outer', suffixes=('', '_3'))
join_final = join_final.rename(columns={'AQI': 'AQI_3'})

# Now columns AQI_0, AQI_1, AQI_2, AQI_3 exist, some may have NaNs

# Aggregate AQI by taking the minimum AQI value across all sources per group
# (min chosen because target examples have AQI values smaller than source max, 
# and min is a safe aggregation to reduce duplicates)

# Create a DataFrame with AQI columns only
aqi_cols = ['AQI_0', 'AQI_1', 'AQI_2', 'AQI_3']

# Replace missing AQI columns with NaN if any missing
for col in aqi_cols:
    if col not in join_final.columns:
        join_final[col] = pd.NA

# Compute min AQI ignoring NaNs
join_final['AQI'] = join_final[aqi_cols].min(axis=1, skipna=True).astype('Int64')

# Select final columns as per target schema
result = join_final[['State Name', 'Year', 'Month', 'AQI']]

# Drop rows with missing values in any of the columns (to match target data)
result = result.dropna(subset=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month', 'AQI'])

# Convert Year and Month to int (if not already)
result['Year'] = result['Year'].astype(int)
result['Month'] = result['Month'].astype(int)
result['AQI'] = result['AQI'].astype(int)

# Sort by State Name, Year, Month for consistency (optional)
result = result.sort_values(by=['State Name', 'Year', 'Month']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_20/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
